2026-08-06-martin-county-sheriffs-office.headline: Missing 14-year-old autistic boy Ethan Boyd safely located, Martin County sheriff says
2026-08-06-martin-county-sheriffs-office.teaser: Ethan Boyd, a missing 14-year-old autistic boy, was safely located at 11:44 p.m., according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office.
2026-08-06-martin-county-sheriffs-office.body:
The Martin County Sheriff’s Office had asked the public for help locating Ethan Boyd, a 14-year-old autistic boy who went missing Wednesday in Palm City. Ethan was last seen at 5:20 p.m. running toward the south side of the Grand Oaks senior living community near Coquina Cove.

Ethan was described as 5 feet 7 inches tall, weighing approximately 130 pounds, with brown hair. He was last seen wearing a dark blue shirt and seafoam green shorts without shoes.

The sheriff’s office asked anyone who saw Ethan to contact deputies immediately. The agency later updated its original Facebook post to announce that he had been safely located.
2026-08-06-martin-county-sheriffs-office.update_text: Ethan Boyd has been safely located, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The agency announced the update in its original Facebook post and thanked the public for sharing information about the missing teenager.

2026-09-29-florida-executes-77-year-old-.headline: Florida set to execute 77-year-old Curtis Beasley at 6 p.m., state's 16th this year
2026-09-29-florida-executes-77-year-old-.teaser: Curtis Wilkie Beasley, 77, is scheduled to be executed by lethal injection at 6 p.m. Tuesday at Florida State Prison for the 1995 murder of Carolyn Monfort.
2026-09-29-florida-executes-77-year-old-.body:
Florida is scheduled to execute Curtis Wilkie Beasley at 6 p.m. Tuesday at Florida State Prison, where the 77-year-old is set to receive a lethal injection for the 1995 murder of Carolyn Monfort. If the execution is carried out, Beasley would become the 16th person executed by Florida this year.

Beasley was convicted of first-degree murder, robbery and grand theft auto in Monfort's death. Prosecutors said he beat Monfort with a hammer at her Dundee home, stole money and her vehicle, and later was arrested in Alabama while using a false identity.

The Florida Supreme Court last week rejected Beasley's latest appeal and denied his request for a stay of execution. His attorneys had argued, among other claims, that executing him at his age while he experiences cognitive decline would violate constitutional protections.

Florida has carried out 15 executions so far in 2026. Beasley's execution remains scheduled for Tuesday evening; a scheduled execution is not treated as completed until state officials confirm that the sentence has been carried out.
2026-09-29-florida-executes-77-year-old-.update_text: An earlier version of this story incorrectly stated that Curtis Beasley had already been executed. His execution is scheduled for 6 p.m. Tuesday.
